title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-arjun-kapoor
content:
Purpose:
Personal debugging scratchpad for recurring GPU OOM / driver mismatch issues seen on dev machines and CI. Keep commands tried, snippets of errors, hypotheses, and actionable next steps.

Background / symptoms observed:
- Model: resnet-style encoder + large LM decoder (seq len 2048) used in local dev and on a few staging nodes.
- Failures happen under larger batch sizes or long context (seq 4096), sometimes after a few iterations (memory fragmentation suspected).
- Two flavors: 1) CUDA OOM from PyTorch, 2) driver / library mismatch errors (cuDNN/CUDA runtime complaints) that manifest after env upgrades or container changes.

Recent reproduction (2026-02-20 staging run):
- Command run (inside docker container):
  docker run --gpus all --rm -it -v /models:/models redwood/serving:staging bash -lc "python serve.py --model /models/large-model --batch 8 --seq-len 4096"
- Error seen (trace snippet):
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.50 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 27.21 GiB already allocated; 1.63 GiB free; 512.00 MiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  
  During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  CUDA error: unknown error

- Immediately before the crash logs: kernel messages in dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 35, GPU has fallen off the bus" (intermittent)

Commands & checks tried (with notes):
1) Check driver / cuda versions on host:
   nvidia-smi
   -- output: Driver Version: 535.86.05  CUDA Version: 12.1
   nvcc --version (in container): NVCC 11.8 (shows mismatch, container has cudatoolkit 11.8)
   NOTE: mismatch between host driver (12.1) and container toolkit (11.8) can be OK (newer driver supports older toolkit), but the reverse is not.

2) Check cuDNN / libcuda loaded libs in container:
   python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
   => prints: 11.7, True (interesting: torch thinks 11.7 despite nvcc 11.8)
   ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(torch._C.__file__)') | grep cudnn
   => shows libcusolver, libcudnn.so.8 -> missing sometimes on minimal containers.

3) Reproduce with reduced batch size / seq length:
   - batch 1, seq 512: runs fine.
   - batch 4, seq 2048: OOM at step ~120 (memory grows over time).
   Hypothesis: KV cache retention + fragmentation; not clearing CUDA cache between inferences.

4) Environment variables experimented:
   - export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
     Observed: reduced fragmentation, but still hit OOM at higher batch.
   - export PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=0 (not relevant on Linux but noted).
   - export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get deterministic stack traces (useful when suspecting driver errors).

5) Mixed precision & gradient checkpointing:
   - Enabled torch.cuda.amp.autocast for inference: memory roughly halved for activations. Good mitigant.
   - Enabled activation checkpointing where applicable -> reduces peak but increases compute.

6) Docker / container checks:
   - Confirmed container runtime is nvidia-container-toolkit v1.12.1.
   - Running "docker run --gpus 'device=0'" vs "--gpus all" showed same result.
   - Tried mounting host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu to container to match drivers -> temporarily resolved "libcuda.so missing" but not sustainable.

7) Kernel logs & GPU flicker (fall off bus) investigation:
   - dmesg shows occasional Xid 35/27 on GPU 0 before crashes. These often indicate GPU hang/kernel driver bug.
   - Repro frequency lower after rebooting host; indicates thermal/driver state could be implicated.

Error snippets collected:
- PyTorch OOM:
  "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.50 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 27.21 GiB already allocated; 1.63 GiB free; 512.00 MiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"

- Driver mismatch / lib complaints (example from CI after image update):
  "Fatal Python error: Aborted
  **
  *** The cuda runtime was unable to initialize: CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE
  ***
  the program has unexpectedly finished.

  /usr/bin/python3: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.11.0: undefined symbol: cuGetProcAddress"

- Xid messages:
  "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 35, GPU has fallen off the bus"

Hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
- Real OOM from model configuration + batch size + long context; exacerbated by fragmentation and KV cache growth.
- Driver/kernel bugs causing GPU hangs (Xid 35) leading to library/runtime errors that look like OOM. Usually correlated with older drivers + heavy kernels.
- Mismatched CUDA runtime vs. host driver in certain container images (libcudart.so from different toolkit causing undefined symbols).
- Memory leak in our custom CUDA kernel or third-party op (less likely but possible).

Actionable mitigations tried & notes:
- Short-term (quick wins):
  - Reduce batch size / sequence length in staging to avoid OOM.
  - Enable FP16 inference (autocast) and activation checkpointing where acceptable.
  - Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to reduce fragmentation.
  - Explicit torch.cuda.empty_cache() between large ops (cheap but not always effective).
- Medium-term:
  - Bake container with matching cudatoolkit to host driver (use CUDA 12.x runtime to match driver 535.x) and pin nvidia-container-toolkit version.
  - Add a startup check to serve.py: verify torch.version.cuda vs nvidia-smi CRC and warn if major mismatch.
  - Instrument memory peaks using torch.cuda.memory_stats() / memory_snapshot() and log to Console/Datadog.
- Long-term / infra:
  - Upgrade staging hosts to driver tested across our images and add driver tests to CI matrix.
  - Add watchdog to detect Xid messages and reboot node or drain GPUs from scheduler.
  - Ensure GPU firmware/drivers across pool are consistent; add image compatibility matrix to deployment docs.

Open experiments / TODOs:
- [ ] Rebuild the staging docker image using CUDA 12.1 base (to match host driver) and run full regen test (batch 8 seq 4096) overnight.
- [x] Try TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tweak (done) — helped a bit.
- [ ] Add a small native test that repeatedly allocs/frees 100MB buffers to stress fragmentation; run under stress to observe leak.
- [ ] File a GitHub issue against third-party op (apex/custom_kernels) if native test reproduces leak.
- [ ] Add automated dmesg/Xid parsing into our node exporter to surface GPU hangs earlier (Ethan assigned).

Useful commands / snippets to reproduce / triage quickly:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
- nvcc --version (in container) and nvidia-smi (host) to compare
- python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count()); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"
- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import torch" 2>&1 | grep cuda || true (shows missing libs at load time)
- export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
- export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1

References / tickets / notes:
- JIRA-4578: "Staging GPU OOMs during long context tests" (linked above)
- GH issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/12345 (similar Xid 35 discussion)
- Confluence: gpu-oom-runbook (draft)

Immediate next steps (my plan):
1) Rebuild staging image with CUDA 12.1 runtime + matching cuDNN and push to staging tag. Run the overnight long-context test.
2) Add startup compatibility check to serve.py to warn and fail-fast if major mismatch detected.
3) Instrument memory stats and log every 50 steps to trace growth.
4) If Xid 35 persists after driver/runtime alignment, escalate to infra to swap GPU (possible HW) and collect full dmesg + syslog for support ticket with vendor.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; copy relevant snippets to JIRA ticket. When closing incident, record final root cause (driver vs config) in Confluence runbook.

-- Arjun
